content:
jordan: Quick q — for incident triage, what's the approved flow for requesting a short-lived SIEM view (read-only) that includes masked PII? Need to hand it to SRE for 4h. Do we still require KMS-wrapped creds for anything? :eyes:

alex: Short answer: yes — use the security-requests queue. Ticket must include justification, index scope, fields needed, and explicit expiry. If you only need masked fields (no raw payloads) 1 approver ok; raw events need 2 approvers.

maya: Also attach the triage playbook/runbook and the sprint/incident link. We create an ephemeral IAM role scoped to the indices and an ephemeral KMS data key only if decryption of encrypted fields is required.

sam: Template below — use it when creating the ticket (paste into the ticket body):

```
Title: JIT SIEM View Request — <short description>
Requester: <name + team>
Oncall/SRE owner: <name>
Scope (indices): <comma-separated indices or query>
Fields requested: <list; mark PII-sensitive>
Purpose/Justification: <why needed>
Expiry (ISO8601): <YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ>
Approvers needed: <1 or 2; mention SOC lead if raw>
Attachments: <runbook link, incident link>
Compliance notes: <any DLP/DPO required?>
Audit tracking ID: auto-populated by bot
```

jordan: perfect — who does the signing-off? tag @sam or someone from sec?

alex: Approvers are SOC lead or security-oncall. For emergencies, sec-oncall can grant JIT up to 8h with a mandatory post-approval review. All approvals and role grants are recorded in the audit log automatically.

sec-bot: [automated] Approval record created: request_id=REQ-2332109876-1, status=pending, ticket_url=https://issues.redwood.ai/REQ-2332109876

maya: Important: no raw exports off the secure network. If an SRE needs to share findings externally, DPO approval + redact/mask step is required.

sam: We'll add a step to the runbook to auto-tag the ticket with TTL and the ephemeral role ARN, and a Lambda to revoke role after expiry. Also emit a CloudTrail event linking role usage to the ticket id.

jordan: can we also include the ephemeral KMS key id in the ticket automatically so auditors can trace decrypts?

alex: yes — when a data key is generated we write key_id to the ticket and to the SIEM audit event. Decrypt operations require the ephemeral role + KMS grant, both logged.

maya: Ok everyone — I'll update the runbook and add the ticket template to the security-requests macro. Will also attach the JIT playbook.

jordan: thanks, that covers it. I'll open one now for the triage run. :thumbsup:
